pages.title: Prophet Noah (pbuh)
pages.content:
Prophet Noah (pbuh) is extensively mentioned in the Holy Qur’an and the hadiths, and he is one of the five great prophets known as the ‘ulul-azm’, or the prophets of great determination. The 71st surah of the Qur’an bears his name and describes his struggle for Tawhid from beginning to end. Since his people, who did not believe in him, were punished by the flood (Tûfan), the flood is also referred to as Noah’s Flood in connection with him.

According to accounts, early generations maintained the belief in the oneness of Allah (Tawhid) until the era of Noah (pbuh). Idolatry first emerged among his people. The prophet was then sent to turn them away from this practice and back to Tawhid. Noah (pbuh) warned his people not to worship anyone other than Allah, and informed them of the punishment that would fall upon them if they did not listen to him (Surah Nûh, 1–4). His people had gone wrong, and they were very cruel and rebellious (Surah az-Zariyat, 46; Surah an-Najm, 52). Consequently, they refused to believe in Noah, even going so far as to call him mad and threaten him with stoning (Surah ash-Shu’ara, 116). In addition to accusing him of lying, they stubbornly demanded that he either remove his poor and humble followers from his presence (Surah al-A’raf, 59–63; Surah Hûd, 27; Surah al-Qamar, 9) or immediately bring the punishment he had warned them about (Surah Hûd, 32).

The Holy Qur’an describes Prophet Noah (pbuh) as a deeply grateful servant (Surah Al-Isra, 3). His patience in the face of adversity has been given as an example to people (Surah Hûd, 49). Another of his characteristics was his firmness toward the disbelievers.

One report (rivayet) says that Noah (pbuh) was the longest-lived of the prophets. The Qur’an provides the following information regarding the age of Prophet Noah: “We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them for a thousand years minus fifty years. Then the Flood swept them; for they were wrongdoers. But We saved him, together with the company of the Ark, and We made it a sign for all peoples.” (Surah Al-Ankabut, 14–15). As understood from this verse, Noah lived with his people for 950 years. However, it is not clear whether this period covers his entire lifespan or the entire period of his prophethood, or only the period until the flood. It is also reported that Noah was the first prophet after Idris (pbuh) and that he worked as a carpenter.

pages.title: The Flood in Ancient Accounts
pages.content:
The oldest accounts of the Flood are found in cuneiform works originating from the Middle East (Sumer, Babylon, Assyria). These ancient texts most closely describe the events narrated in sacred texts. The earliest written records date back to the Sumerians. In Sumer and Akkad, the flood is remembered as one of the greatest catastrophes in human history.

In the Sumerian version, King Ziusudra, according to the tablet, was told that a flood was coming and was asked to build a ship. The Flood covered the land for seven days and seven nights. Ziusudra survived the flood by building an ark. In addition to the Sumerian tablet, another fragment, consisting of just a few lines and written in Old Babylonian, was found that describes the flood. The most complete description of the flood story from the Babylonians is found in the Epic of Gilgamesh (Gılgamış Destanı).

In the epic, the story develops as follows: after the death of his best friend, Gilgamesh, King of Uruk, experiences profound grief. He aims to find Uta-napishtim (also known in Sumerian as Ziusudra), who survived the flood and attained immortality. Gilgamesh hopes to bring his friend back to life and learn the secret of immortality from Uta-napishtim. Uta-napishtim tells him the story of the flood. As the king of a city on the banks of the Euphrates, he explains how the gods, troubled by the excessive noise of humankind, wished to destroy the human race with a flood. However, the god Ea warns Uta-napiştim and tells him to build a ship to save his family and a certain number of animals. The Flood begins with a pouring rain, and this rain lasts six days and seven nights. On the seventh day, the storm stops and the ship lands on Mount Nisir. Thus, everyone on board is saved. Archaeological research suggests that Sumer and Akkad were severely affected by devastating floods.

pages.title: The Flood in the Qur’an
pages.content:
The word ‘Tûfan’ appears in two places in the Holy Qur’an. In one instance, it refers to the flood that happened to Pharaoh and the people of Egypt (Surah Al-A‘râf, 133), and in the other, to the flood that hit Noah’s people (Surah Al-Ankabut, 14).

According to the Qur’an, the Flood was directed at the unbelievers among Noah’s people, and it was sent to punish them. Allah commanded Noah to build an ark, informing him that his people, who had rejected the truth, would be destroyed by the flood, while he and the believers would be saved (Surah Hûd, 36–39).

The Qur’an states only that Noah’s ark was made of pieces of wood and fastened with nails (Surah al-Qamar, 13).

Influenced by Sumerian and Babylonian accounts, the Torah states that Noah’s Flood covered the entire world. This issue has been debated, and various views have been put forward regarding whether Noah’s Flood was global or local in extent.

According to the Holy Qur’an, however, Prophet Noah was sent as a prophet to his people (Surah Ash-Shu’ara, 106), and the flood came to punish those among Noah’s people who did not believe (Surah A’raf, 59–64; Surah Hûd, 25–49; Surah Furqan, 37; Surah Shu’ara, 105–122; Surah Qamar, 9–16). Therefore, extending a catastrophe which was brought upon the unbelievers of a single people to the entire world and destroying all living creatures because of a few unbelievers is contrary to divine justice. The only prophet sent to humanity is the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Based on this, the view that the flood was specific only to the region where Noah lived and that the animals taken on to the ark were domesticated animals from Noah’s own farm is generally accepted.

pages.title: The Idols of Noah’s People
pages.content:
As narrated by Ibn Abbas, who was one of the companions of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and a leading figure in the fields of tafsir and fiqh, the Prophet (pbuh) said: “The period between Adam and Noah was ten centuries.” (İbn Sa’d et-Tabakâtû’l-Kübrâ, Beyrut t.y., I, 42)

For many generations, Noah’s people had worshiped statues that they considered to be gods. They believed these gods to provide for all of their needs, bring them prosperity, and protect them from harm.

In the Qur’an, Allah tells us that Noah’s people said: “Do not abandon your gods; do not leave your ilâhs, namely Wad, Suwa’, Yaghus, Ya’uk, and Nasr” (Surah Nûh, 23). These were the idols worshipped by Noah’s people. Initially, these were the names of righteous individuals who had lived among them and displayed exceptional good deeds. After their deaths, statues were made of them, and later people turned them into objects of worship and used them as mediators between themselves and Allah. Following generations just knew that their parents had prayed to them; they had no idea why they had been built. This is how idolatry developed.

Ibn Abbas explained: The names (of the idols) formerly belonged to some pious men of the people of Noah, and when they died, Satan inspired their people to prepare and place idols at the places where they used to sit, and to call those idols by their names. The people did so, but the idols were not worshipped until those who made them died and their origin was forgotten; after that, people began to worship them. (Sahih al-Bukhari 4920, Tafseer 65, Hadith 440)

pages.title: Noah Calls His People
pages.content:
In such circumstances, Allah sent Noah with His message to his people. Noah was an extremely patient man and a great speaker. He tirelessly spoke to his people about the power of Allah. He kept saying that the day always comes after the night and that Allah created the harmony between these opposites for our benefit. While the day provides warmth and encourages activity, the night offers coolness and relaxation. While the moon and stars help with the measurement of time, direction, and seasons, the sun fosters growth and keeps all plants and animals alive.

He told them that only Allah is the rightful owner of the land and the heavens, thus there could not have been more than one creator. He told them that worshipping idols was unfair to the human mind because it restricted thinking freely. It does not make sense to worship a handmade object as a superior being when you carved it yourself from stone, wood, or metal. This false belief limits a person’s potential and free will and leads people to blind faith. In a sense, this means the enslavement of human beings.

He also kept warning them about the severe consequences they would face if they insisted on their wrongdoing. Whenever Noah would come while they were worshipping idols and say, “La ilaha illallah,” they would either run away or wrap their clothes around their heads and put their fingers in their ears so as not to hear what the Prophet was saying. Throughout his mission, his people treated him with every kind of cruelty and beat him nearly to death. However, he never abandoned his path. As soon as he recovered, he returned to his mission. For centuries, he was exposed to stoning, humiliation, and oppression.

Prophet Noah’s warning divided his community into opposing camps. While the wealthy and powerful rejected his message, his consoling message offered comfort, hope, and healing to society’s most vulnerable group of people. The elites wanted things to stay the same, so they started arguing with Noah. Initially, they argued that Noah was just an ordinary person like them.

“The chiefs of the disbelievers among his people said: ‘We see you but a man like ourselves.’” (Surah Hûd, verse 27)

Indeed, he affirmed that he was only a human. He explained that Allah sent a human prophet to guide the people because humans populate the earth. If the earth were full of angels, then Allah would have sent an angel messenger instead. At first, the ruling class ignored Noah’s message, supposing it would fade out. However, when his teachings gained ground among the society’s poor, helpless, and manual laborers, the elites felt threatened. They responded by mocking him and verbally attacking his followers as “worthless outsiders.”

Allah said in the Holy Qur’an:

“Indeed We sent Noah to his people (he said): ‘I have come to you as a plain Warner that you worship none but Allah, surely, I fear for you the torment of a painful Day.’ The chiefs of the disbelievers among his people said: ‘We see you but a man like ourselves, nor do we see any follow you but the meanest among us and they too followed you without thinking. And we do not see in you any merit above us in fact we think you are liars.’” (Surah Hûd, verses 25–27).

pages.title: The Wealthy Elite and the Poor Believers
pages.content:
The wealthy elite demanded that Noah (pbuh) abandon his poor, humble, gentle, and patient followers as a condition for their faith. Noah (pbuh) refused to make concessions and gently explained that the believers served Allah and it was not his right to drive them away. He then appealed to their reason and faith and invited them to embrace the truth.

“O my people! I ask of you no wealth for it, my reward is from none but Allah. I am not going to drive away those who have believed. Surely, they are going to meet their Lord, but I see that you are a people that are ignorant. O my people! Who will help me against Allah, if I drove them away? Will you not then give a thought? And I do not say to you that with me are the Treasures of Allah nor that I know the unseen, nor do I say I am an angel, and I do not say of those whom your eyes look down upon that Allah will not bestow any good on them. Allah knows what is in their inner selves (regards to Belief). In that case, I should, indeed be one of the Zalimeen (wrongdoers, oppressors etc).” (Surah Hûd, verses 29-31)

Prophet Noah (pbuh) used the true wisdom given by Allah to prove the disbelievers wrong. This shows a totally logical way of thinking that ignores one’s personal ego and selfish desires to focus only on the truth.

vocabulary.definition: Something good given for a good action.
Think that someone is less important than you.

pages.title: Nine Hundred and Fifty Years
pages.content:
Allah related about them:

They said: “O Noah! You have disputed with us and much have you prolonged the dispute with us, now bring upon us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful.” He said: “Only Allah will bring it (the punishment) on you, if He will, and then you will escape not. And my advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to give you counsel, if Allah’s Will is to keep you astray. He is your Lord! And to Him you shall return.” (Surah Hûd, verses 32-34)

The conflict went on, and the debates between Noah and the unbelievers grew more intense. The unbelievers started acting rudely and insulting Allah’s prophet after all of their arguments failed and they had nothing more to say.

“The leaders of his people said: ‘Verily, we see you in plain error.’” (Surah A’râf, verse 60)

In response, Noah answered calmly, as prophets do.

“O my people! There is no error in me, but I am a Messenger from the Lord of the Worlds (mankind, jinn and all that exists)! I convey to you the Messages of my Lord and give sincere advice to you. And I know from Allah what you know not.” (Surah A’râf, verses 61-62)

Noah (pbuh) went on to call his people to believe in Allah for 950 years.

Every generation that followed was warned not to believe Noah (pbuh) and to fight against him.

At some point, Noah (pbuh) received a revelation from Allah that no one else would accept his invitation. (See Surah Hûd, verse 36) When Allah advised him to stop grieving for them, Noah (pbuh) prayed for the destruction of the unbelievers, so they would not mislead the people. Now that the Prophet’s suffering had finally reached its limit, he turned to Allah in prayer.

Noah (pbuh) said: “My Lord! Leave not one of the disbelievers on the earth. If You leave them, they will mislead Your slaves and they will give birth only to wicked sinners” (Surah Nûh, verses 26–27)

Noah’s prayer was accepted. The case was resolved, and He delivered His judgment on the disbelievers through a flood. Allah commanded His servant Noah (pbuh) to construct an ark based on His knowledge and instructions.

Allah commanded: “And construct the ship under Our Eyes and with Our Inspiration and address Me not on behalf of those who did wrong; they are surely to be drowned.” (Surah Hûd, verse 37)

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Answering Calmly
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write eight to ten sentences about why answering insults calmly is wise.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happens when people answer anger with anger?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “Answering insults calmly is wise because anger rarely changes anyone’s mind. In Chapter 7, Noah answered calmly even after the leaders said he was in plain error. When people answer anger with anger, a small argument quickly grows more intense. For example, after a football match, two classmates started shouting at each other. Their teacher spoke quietly, and both of them slowly calmed down. Now that I have seen this, I try to wait a few seconds before I answer. Calm words protect friendships. They also show strength, not weakness.”

pages.title: Noah Builds the Ark
pages.content:
Noah (pbuh) chose a remote location far from the sea. After gathering wood and essential tools, he worked tirelessly day and night to construct the ark. The people kept making fun of him: “Noah, did you give up being a prophet just to build things as a carpenter? Why are you building a huge ark out here far from the sea anyway? How is it going to reach the water? Are you going to drag it yourself, or is the wind supposed to move it for you?”

Allah said in the Qur’an: “As he was constructing the ship, whenever the chiefs of his people passed by him, they made a mockery of him. He said: ‘If you mock at us, so do we mock at you likewise for your mocking. And you will know who it is on whom will come a torment that will cover him with disgrace and on whom will fall a lasting torment.’” (Surah Hûd, verses 38–39)

vocabulary.definition: Pull something heavy along the ground.

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write eight to ten sentences about how mockery affects people and how they can respond.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “People often mock new ideas because they do not understand them. In Chapter 8, the people kept making fun of Noah while he built the ark far from the sea. Many inventors faced the same reaction. Is a new idea supposed to be popular from the first day? pages.title: The Flood Begins
pages.content:
Once Noah (pbuh) finished building the ark, he waited for Allah’s command. Allah told him that the flood would begin, and that it was time to take action, the moment water, according to a report, started to overflow from the oven of a woman baking bread.

The dreadful day finally came when the oven overflowed, so he hurried to open the ark and call upon the believers.

He brought along one male and one female of every kind of animal, bird, and insect. Watching him take the creatures toward the ark, the crowd started laughing and said, “Noah must have lost his mind! What is he going to do with all those animals?”

Allah narrated: “So it was till then there came Our Command and the fountains of the earth gushed forth! We said: ‘Board into it a pair of each kind two (male and female), and your family, except him against whom the Word has already gone forth, and those who believe.’ And none believed him except a few.” (Surah Hûd, verse 40)

pages.title: The Number of Believers
pages.content:
Noah’s wife and one of his sons rejected his message and refused to join him on the ark. While the wife openly disbelieved, the son rejected his father’s faith. In the same way, the majority of people refused to believe it and chose not to get on the boat.

Islamic scholars hold different views on how many people were on the ark with Noah (pbuh). While Ibn Abbas noted there were 80 believers, some mentioned the number was 72. Meanwhile, other accounts suggest there were only 10 people with him.

pages.title: The Flood
pages.content:
Water rose from every crack in the earth, and not a single crack was left dry, as an unprecedented downpour fell from the sky. Heavy rain fell for hours while water burst from cracks in the ground, causing the water level to rise constantly. Soon, ocean waves covered the land. A strange movement deep inside the earth pushed the ocean floor upward, flooding the dry ground.

Noah (pbuh) said, “Embark in it. In the name of Allah shall be its sailing and its stop. My Lord is indeed Forgiving and Merciful.” And so it sailed with them amidst waves like hills. And Noah called to his son, who had kept away, “O my son! Embark with us, and do not be with the disbelievers.” He said, “I will take refuge on a mountain—it will protect me from the water.” He said, “There is no protection from Allah’s decree today, except for him on whom He has mercy.” And the waves came in between them, and he was among the drowned. (Surah Hûd, verses 41–43)

“And it was said, ‘O earth, swallow your waters,’ and ‘O heaven, clear up.’ And the waters receded, and the event was concluded, and the ark settled on Judi, and it was proclaimed: ‘Away with the wicked people.’” (Surah Hûd, verse 44)

After Allah gave the command, peace returned to the world, the floodwaters went down, and the sun shone on the dry ground once again. The great flood cleared the land of those who worshipped many gods.

pages.title: The Believers Come Ashore and Ashura
pages.content:
Noah (pbuh) released the birds and animals to spread across the earth, and then the believers stepped off the ark safe and sound. Noah put his forehead to the ground in prostration. The survivors then gathered around a fire they had just made. This was a great relief, as starting a fire was banned on the ship in order to prevent the ship from catching fire. During the whole journey, none of them had the chance to eat hot food.

Noah (pbuh) and those with him disembarked from the ark on the tenth day of the month of Muharram (Ashura). For their safe and sound survival of the Flood and their arrival on dry land, they fasted on that day to give thanks to Allah. Ashura has existed since the time of Prophet Noah (pbuh), and it is a day on which the pre-Islamic Arabs had been fasting since the time of Prophet Abraham (pbuh). Aisha (Âişe), the daughter of Abu Bakr and wife of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), narrated this as follows: “Ashura was a day on which the Quraysh used to fast during the pre-Islamic era. The Messenger of Allah also followed this fasting tradition. When he migrated to Medina, he continued this fast and commanded others to do so as well. However, once the fast of Ramadan was made obligatory, he himself stopped fasting on the day of Ashura; from then on, Muslims were free to fast on this day if they wished, or not to fast if they chose” (Bukhari, “Sawm,” 69; Musnad, VI, 29–30). Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) recommended fasting either on the 9th and 10th or on the 10th and 11th of Muharram. (Musnad, 2154; Sahih Ibn Huzayme, 2095.)

pages.title: Noah’s Last Advice
pages.content:
The Qur’an concludes Noah’s narrative, leaving us without details about his later interactions with his people. According to a hadith, before he passed away, he advised his sons to worship Allah alone.

Abdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀs narrated that the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said: “When the death of the Messenger of Allah Noah approached, he admonished his sons: 'Indeed I would give you far reaching advice, commanding you to do two things, and warning you against doing two things as well. I charge you to believe that there is no god but Allah and that if the seven heavens and the seven earths were put on one side of a scale and the words ‘there is no god but Allah’ were put on the other, the latter would outweigh the former. I warn you against associating partners with Allah and against pride.’” (Müsned, II, 169; Buhari, Edebu’l-Mufred) (Ahmad, al-Musnad, 2:169)

The Prophet’s final words summarize the struggle he waged.

exercises.title: Notice: How Certain Is the Writer?
exercises.instructions: Sort the statements: presented as certain, or presented carefully as a report or a view?
exercises.question: How certain is the writer?

items: The 71st surah of the Qur’an bears his name.
The word ‘Tûfan’ appears in two places in the Holy Qur’an.
Archaeological research suggests that Sumer and Akkad were severely affected by devastating floods.
Other accounts suggest there were only 10 people with him.

Presented as certain: The 71st surah of the Qur’an bears his name.
The word ‘Tûfan’ appears in two places in the Holy Qur’an.
Presented carefully: Archaeological research suggests that Sumer and Akkad were severely affected by devastating floods.
Other accounts suggest there were only 10 people with him.

exercises.explanation: Facts from the text of the Qur’an are stated directly. “Suggests”, “according to a report” and “it is not clear whether” show careful reporting.

feedback.correct: Good. You noticed how certain the writer is.
feedback.incorrect: Look for suggests and according to.

exercises.title: Notice: Formal Verb Forms
exercises.instructions: Choose the sentence with the correct formal form.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The elite demanded that Noah abandon his followers.
The elite demanded that Noah abandons his followers.
The elite demanded that Noah to abandon his followers.
exercises.explanation: After “demand that”, formal English uses the base form of the verb (the subjunctive).

feedback.incorrect: Which verb form follows demand that?

exercises.title: Notice: Deduction
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: In “Noah must have lost his mind!”, the crowd is expressing an obligation.
exercises.explanation: “Must have + past participle” expresses a confident deduction about the past, not an obligation.

feedback.correct: Correct. It is a deduction, and a wrong one.
feedback.incorrect: Is it a guess or a rule?

exercises.explanation: “While” shows a contrast, “consequently” a result, and “now that” a reason based on a new situation.

feedback.incorrect: Is it a contrast, a result or a reason?

feedback.correct: Correct. So as not to hear, associating, is.

exercises.explanation: Unprecedented, remote, determination and obligatory come from the book. Here they describe a rescue team today.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s words in a new text.
feedback.incorrect: Read the words around each gap.

exercises.title: Use: Check a Short Text

errorItems.sentence: Our teacher demanded that every student brings a dictionary.
The rules prevent students to use phones in class.

exercises.explanation: Use the base form after “demand that”, “prevent … from + -ing” and “in addition to + -ing”.

feedback.incorrect: Check the subjunctive and the prepositions.

exercises.title: Use: Patience, Justice and Humility Today
exercises.instructions: Write eight to ten sentences arguing which lesson from Noah’s story matters most today. Use evidence and one counterpoint.
exercises.question: Which lesson matters most? Why?
exercises.explanation: Example: “I would argue that the most important lesson from Noah’s story is justice for the weak. In Chapter 6, the wealthy elite demanded that Noah abandon his poor followers, but he refused to make concessions. Today, people are still sometimes judged by their wealth. Some might argue that patience is a more important lesson, because Noah called his people for 950 years. However, patience without justice would not have protected the poor believers. Noah’s refusal shows that faith and fairness go together. Consequently, I believe schools and communities should treat every person with equal respect.”

feedback.correct: Check: a position, evidence, a counterpoint and a conclusion.
